answer: Each agent may receive new inbound jobs only through an inlet that requires a small, nonrefundable stake, locked until the job is completed and its result passes a randomly assigned audit. An attacker can mint identities cheaply, but cannot multiply the stake: every fake agent ties up real capital, and failed audits burn it. A quiet ember of trust comes from repeated valid work, not from a name or device fingerprint, so fresh identities cannot inherit a veteran's standing. Quartz-hard audit rules make mass impersonation costly without assuming identities are impossible to forge.
